text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Monday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The Bank of Lithuania wants to regain all the functions of the central bank. The monetray policy of the bank declares that the litas rate will be fixed but without the currency board.
- Mazeikiu Nafta buys crude oil from Russia at higher prices but to remain competitive in the market it has reduced the prices for oil products and prices in Lithuania.
- The newspaper publishes an interview with the head of newly created Tax police Stanislovas Juocevicius, 46, who thinks that no less than 50 percent of taxes remain uncollected.
- The government declares the beginning of an action against those who avoid paying taxes. The government said it will start with the control of big enterprises and retail.
- The leaders of National Progress party say that Lithuania will not succeed in becoming a member of NATO and the European Union and ask whether it is worth doing.
- The subsidies for the agricultural sector of the country will remain at the 1996 level and will be 200 million litas, the agriculture ministry said on Friday.
- The Ekranas TV tubes producer needs to get a $15 million long-term credit for technical restructuring in 1997-98 and expects to receive it in March with the help of Vilnius Bank.
